noReleases.message: Flotilla hasn’t been released yet. Watch the project on GitHub to hear when it is.
noReleases.watchHint: To hear about new versions, choose Watch › Custom › Releases on GitHub.

common.firstLaunchBlocked: Flotilla isn’t notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time you open it, with a warning that Apple couldn’t verify it’s free of malware.

accessibility.settingsPath: You can turn it on in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility. On macOS 27, that page is Privacy & Security › Device Control and Data Access.
accessibility.reenable: Flotilla is ad-hoc signed, so you may need to turn this permission on again after an update.

withoutAccessibility.nearPointer: The panel opens near the pointer and may not line up with the group icon
withoutAccessibility.slower: It takes a little longer to appear after you click

meta.title: Flotilla — Keep your Dock organized.
meta.description: Group apps, files, folders, and web pages in your Mac’s Dock. Free and open source, for Macs with Apple silicon running macOS 15 or later.

hero.title: Keep your Dock organized.
hero.lead: Group apps, files, folders, and web pages in your Mac’s Dock.
hero.screenshotAlt: The Essentials group open above the Dock, showing apps and a folder in a grid, with an arrow pointing to the group icon

statement: The Dock’s own folders can only sit on the right.
Flotilla puts groups on the left, next to your apps.

groups.title: Flotilla groups
groups.position: On the left, next to your apps

highlights.noFolders: Grouping doesn’t move your apps or files, and there are no folders to create on disk.
highlights.mixedItems: Apps, files, folders, and web pages can all go in the same group.
highlights.nativeGrid: Click a group icon and it opens in a grid that looks and animates just like a Dock folder.

features.title: Organize apps, files, and web pages.

folders.title: Browse folders in place
folders.description: Like a Dock stack, a folder opens right in the panel, with file thumbnails. To see it in Finder instead, click Open in Finder at the end of the grid.
folders.backButton: Click the back button to go up a level
folders.hiddenFiles: Turn on Show hidden files in Settings to see hidden files too
folders.screenshotAlt: The Wallpapers folder open in the panel, showing image thumbnails and Open in Finder at the end

dragAndDrop.title: Drag and drop
dragAndDrop.description: Drop apps, files, and folders onto a group icon in the Dock, or onto a group in the settings window, to add them. Web pages can be dragged from your browser into the settings window.

settings.title: Manage groups in the settings window
settings.add: Click Add… to pick apps, files, folders, or web pages
settings.rename: Double-click a group to rename it
settings.reorder: Drag items to reorder them or move them into another group
settings.moreOptions: Right-click or Control-click an item for more options

nestedGroups.title: Groups within groups
nestedGroups.description: Put groups inside other groups. A subgroup opens right in the same panel, and the back button takes you back up.

iconPreviews.title: Group icon previews
iconPreviews.description: The group icon shows its first few items, up to four. You can change how many in Settings. Its background follows light and dark mode.

reorderAndRemove.title: Reorder and remove
reorderAndRemove.description: Drag items in the panel to reorder them. To remove one, drag it out of the panel and let go once Remove appears.

tracking.title: Keeps track of your items
tracking.description: Apps and files still open after you move or rename them. And when an app updates, the group opens the new version.

background.title: Menu bar app
background.description: Flotilla runs from the menu bar, so it doesn’t add its own icon to the Dock. Opening a panel doesn’t take focus away from the app you’re using.

languages.title: Eight languages
languages.description: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French, and Spanish. Flotilla follows your system language and falls back to English for any other.

howItWorks.title: What does Flotilla change on your Mac?
howItWorks.lead: The left side of the Dock only takes apps, so Flotilla gives each top-level group a placeholder app with the group’s name and icon, and adds that to the Dock.

dockIcons.title: Only its own group icons
dockIcons.preferences: Flotilla adds group icons by editing the Dock preferences (com.apple.dock).
dockIcons.scope: It only touches its own entries in persistent-apps, the app section of the Dock, and leaves your other icons and Dock settings alone.

backup.title: A backup before any change
backup.description: Each time Flotilla launches, it backs up com.apple.dock before its first change. It keeps the 5 most recent backups.

dockRestart.title: The Dock restarts for a moment
dockRestart.description: To apply a change, Flotilla ends the Dock process and macOS restarts it.
dockRestart.triggers: Group icon updates need a restart too, for example when a group’s first few items change or your Mac switches between light and dark mode.

data.title: Data and settings
data.location: Flotilla keeps its data in ~/Library/Application Support/Flotilla:
data.dockTiles: DockTiles/: the placeholder apps for top-level groups
data.settings: Settings live in the com.rakuyo.flotilla preferences domain.

network.title: Network access
network.description: Flotilla only goes online to fetch a web page’s title when you add or edit one, and to check for and download updates from GitHub Releases. You can turn automatic checks off under Software Update in Settings.

openSource.title: The code and the conversation are on GitHub.
openSource.lead: Flotilla is free and open source. Read the code, report a problem, or pitch in on GitHub.

follow.title: Follow the project
follow.description: If you like Flotilla, a star on GitHub is always welcome. To hear about new versions, choose Watch › Custom › Releases.

issues.title: Report a problem
issues.description: Something not working? Open an issue on GitHub.

blocked.question: Why does macOS block Flotilla the first time I open it?
blocked.openAnyway: Click Done, open System Settings › Privacy & Security, and click Open Anyway under Security. The button is only there for an hour after you try to open Flotilla.

withoutAccessibility.question: Can I use Flotilla without Accessibility access?

reenable.question: Why might I need to turn on Accessibility access again after an update?

removeIcon.question: How do I take a group icon out of the Dock, and can I put it back?
removeIcon.remove: Just drag the group icon out of the Dock.
removeIcon.addBack: That only removes the icon. The group stays in the settings window, marked Not in Dock, until you right-click it and choose Add to Dock.

steps.unzip: Unzip the download and drag Flotilla.app into Applications
steps.accessibility: Turn on Accessibility access in System Settings

install.title: Install Flotilla and set it up.

unzip.title: Unzip it and move it to Applications
unzip.description: Double-click the downloaded Flotilla-X.Y.Z.zip to unzip it, then drag Flotilla.app into your Applications folder.
unzip.note: Finder shows the app’s name in your system language. In Simplified Chinese, for example, it’s 归帆.

firstLaunch.title: Open it for the first time
firstLaunch.openAnyway: Scroll down to Security, find the message about Flotilla, and click Open Anyway
firstLaunch.openAnywayNote: The button is only there for an hour after you try to open Flotilla
firstLaunch.done: From then on, Flotilla opens normally.
firstLaunch.terminal: If you’d rather use Terminal, remove the quarantine attribute with this command instead, then open Flotilla:

why.question: Why does macOS block Flotilla?
why.answer: Flotilla is ad-hoc signed and isn’t notarized by Apple, so macOS shows a security warning the first time you open it.
appleGuide: Apple explains these checks, and how to open an app anyway, in

accessibility.title: Turn on Accessibility access
accessibility.purpose: Flotilla uses Accessibility access to read the Dock’s interface, so it can:
accessibility.locate: Find the group icon and line the panel up with it
accessibility.openOnRelease: Open the panel as soon as you release the mouse button, just like a Dock folder
accessibility.prompt: Until you grant access, macOS asks for it the first time you click a group icon after each launch.

reenable.title: You may need to turn it on again

files.title: Files and folders
files.description: The first time you open a folder in Documents, Desktop, Downloads, or a similar location from a panel, macOS asks whether Flotilla can access it. Flotilla can only show what’s inside once you allow it.

copyButton.copied: Copied. Paste it into Terminal to run it
copyButton.label: Copy

getStarted.title: Create your first group.
getStarted.lead: Click the sailing ship in the menu bar and choose Settings… to manage your groups. Quit Flotilla is in the same menu.

create.title: Create a group
create.newGroup: Under Groups, click New Group, type a name, and press Return
create.newGroupNote: The Dock restarts for a moment, then the group icon shows up next to your apps
create.add: Select the group, click Add…, and choose Add Apps…, Add Files…, or Add Web Page…
create.drop: You can also drag apps, files, and folders onto a group in the settings window or onto its icon in the Dock. Web pages can be dragged from your browser into the settings window

panel.title: Use the panel
panel.open: Click a group icon in the Dock, then click the app, file, or web page you want to open
panel.browse: Click a subgroup or folder to open it, and use the back button to go up a level
panel.close: To close the panel, click the group icon again, click outside the panel, or press Esc
panel.remove: To remove an item, drag it out of the panel and let go once Remove appears

getStarted.readme: The full guide is in the README
